A Noted Policeman

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We look at SA Idols winner - Tapelo Molomo

Unique Selling Point:
A warrant officer working in the district of the North West, is making a difference in the SAPS, big time. After witnessing the struggles of the cops, and what they have to deal with mentally, everyday, he decided to become a trauma counellor. We follow Warrant officer and Idols winner, Thapelo Molomo and see the how police officers cope with trauma everyday.

Summary:
We have countless stories regarding corrupt cops. This time we peak behind the scenes and discover mental strain our officers are facing everyday fighting crime.

Further information:
Thapelo Molomo, is a 29-year-old police officer, who hails from the streets of Dipetsaneng Village, close to Mokopane in Limpopo Province, is now working with colleagues to improve their wellness and treat the trauma they have to deal with, day in and day out.
But he has another talent… He can sing!
He has a burning passion for music, which is the driving force behind his participation in the 2022 Idols SA Competition, and he won!

Script:


Early morning Drone opening over Tembisa
AUDIO: Hustling and bustling of a busy corner on the road. People selling stuff.
VO:
We're in Tembisa, on Joburg’s East Rand, where street vendors try to make a living, selling goods to people heading to work, early in the morning.
This story is about seizing the moment... about resilience when dreams take long to materialise... and above all, a story of hope!
Link:
One of these VENDORs has achieved really great heights because of a particular talent that he has. …and if you listen carefully, you might just hear it…

(Molomo Singing whilst selling)

VO: Believe it or not, that voice is worth a Million Rand!
Break and Idols Announcement
VO: The winner of SA Idols is… Thapelo!!!
VO: When Thapelo Molomo was given the chance to enter Idols, he grabbed the opportunity with both hands! After weeks of gruelling competition he was finally announced Idols winner in November last year. But there is more to Thapelo than what meets the ear…
Thapelo: I am a Warrant officer, I am a singer, a trauma counsellor by profession, an Idol winner, and I am very famous now!
Link: Achieving fame and fortune on stage might have been a dream, but it's not the purpose that fuels his life!
Thapelo: We are selling eggs and atchar, as a way of saying to the young people: instead of sitting at home and saying there's no work, just do something for yourself, inspiring the young people, that here we are, I just won Idols, and I don't mind getting myself dirty on the streets, just to expand my stream of income. Just to motivate them, you know, people in the entertainment industry, as a way of showing them that it doesn't matter where you are, just do something, take what you got, invest it somewhere, so that when the dry season comes , you know you are good to go.
VO: Apart from an Idols winner, Thapelo is also a full time S.A.P.S. Warrant Officer, based in the Brits area, in the North West Province. Working as a Trauma counsellor in the Employee health and wellness program, he knows all too well, the trauma S.A.P.S. members are facing everyday.
Xola:
You're exposed to things that normal people ordinarily don't come across, what does that do to someone's psyche?
Thapelo: It affects them a lot, I think that's why we are there as trauma counsellors, to really assist them to handle the the the all the trauma they face, because they are human beings as well, and like any other human being, if you see something traumatic, it definitely affects you and you somehow need some sort of a support to cope with what you've witnessed, so we assist them to have that emotional containment, also, we give them the space to vent out their frustrations, what they witnessed, all the fears and so forth.
The job that he does for S.A.P.S., he's also practising it in our community as well.
VO: Thapelo applies his skills wherever needed. And in a village just outside Rustenburg his friend, Lebogang Mpane, shares with us, the challenges they face.
Lebogang: I have got a lot of kids doing drugs, Nyaopi, all those things, I’ll always call him and say, Thapelo, please come in assist and give them counselling, and he always does, he always makes time to come in and advise us, to stop doing drugs and he’s marvellous and that as well.
Thapelo: I'm passionate about the community. It is all about motivation and remind them what is possible. They normally have role models, but the role models they don't come closer to them, have the role models, I felt it is important to come closer to them and show them that it is possible, that we are here…
VO: And this is no more evident than here in Tembisa, where Thapelo went to school. He planned a surprise visit to one of the schools, to offer some advice to the Grade 12s.
Break
Thapelo is driven to bring change, especially to the youth.
Thapelo: It all begins at school. You can change something in your family provided you take your education very seriously. So I'm here to motivate you guys to really push and work hard for yourself and do well. If I can do it you can also do it you can also do it, you get it né?
Mabel:
It's important for children to have a role model, the knowledge that you impart not only to the children but to adults as well.
VO: Mabel Sikhakhane is the principal of Nokuphila Primary School and a community leader. She encourages the public to get involved in their local schools, to add value to the lives of vulnerable children.

Mabel: Children in the communities learn morals and values from teachers, even their role models as adults, as people who are stars and celebrities, they take them as celebrities, they're still learning, so they will say, I will learn and I will want to be like so and so. Education is the key To Success.
XOLA: The young people are incredibly receptive. They obviously want to hear from somebody like Thapelo, somebody that they look up to, and somebody that they can emulate.
Thapelo: The youth, to me, is very important, because I know the power that we have, the little motivation that I've bring up to them, because I know after they receive their type of motivation they are able to run and change the world.
Thapelo: I use my fame by motivating people, to see transformation in people's life. Be it mental health the it financially. I use my fame by motivating people to see transformation in people’s lives, and that would be me, actually bringing that assistance of change to them, that makes me happy!
LINK: Thapelo is a very busy man, we followed him from Tembisa to Rustenburg and now, a studio in Randburg
VO: He is adding the final touches to a song that will be released soon, and that is all thanks to his Idols win.
XHOLA: Your name was called out as a winner, do you remember that moment?
Thapelo: I remember it very clearly, when they said Thapelo, it was quite a great feeling. But more than anything, I was very much contained. I always knew I was going to make it, because of my faith. I used to pray a lot. Even the contestants will actually tell you, that one was always praying. I was that type of contestant.
Xola: Do You have any advice for people who find themselves in a tough space?
Thapelo: I believe that if we can look at the situation as a temporary situation not permanently, you can actually outgrow that situation, be it employment, do something like I'm selling eggs now. I'm trying to send that message to somebody that, let's not spend time feeling sorry for ourselves, let's find ways of getting out of those dark spaces we are facing.
LINK:
Having spent some time with Thapelo, it's very clear to see that he cares about people and about making a real connection. Between the smiles and the selfies, it really is an inspiration and it inspires people to do better, to be better, to be a little like Thapelo, and if we were, the world would be a kinder place.
